concerns.text: T017 implements the Shapiro-Wilk pre-check and Wilcoxon fallback for FR-006, but omits the mandatory 'bootstrapped confidence intervals' requirement for sensitivity analysis runs (varying split ratios). This is a semantic weakening of FR-006's acceptance criteria.

T023 is scoped only to 'Comparison logic for Bayesian vs. Isotonic'. FR-006 requires the Diebold-Mariano test to compare the baseline against *each* recalibrated method (Baseline vs. Isotonic, Baseline vs. Bayesian, Isotonic vs. Bayesian). The Baseline vs. Bayesian comparison is missing from the task list, violating the requirement to compare all methods.

T020 specifies a 'lead-time decay prior' but fails to explicitly task the implementation of the 'structured prior that respects the physics of forecast degradation' mandated by FR-005 and US-3. Without explicit instruction on the physics-respecting structure (e.g., specific functional form), the task risks implementing a generic prior, violating the constitutional constraint on meteorological integrity.

T015 focuses on 'handling sparse lead times' but does not explicitly mandate iteration over *variables* (precipitation and temperature) as required by FR-004 ('for each lead time and variable'). This risks a task that only handles lead-time stratification, failing to satisfy the full scope of the functional requirement.

T021 mentions 'short chains, 2 chains' but omits the explicit constraint on the *number of draws* (e.g., 500 as per Spec Assumption) required to meet SC-005 (runtime ≤ 30 mins). Without this explicit tasking, the implementation may use default PyMC draw counts, violating the performance constraint.
